groups.label: “Shut in” after Dennis died, until the dog opened the door
groups.description: A still house come alive with someone in it to tell, and a reason to get up, eat and be among people again

groups.label: Holding on to Pepper, and to her own say over her life
groups.description: After the fall and her daughter's “the dog has to go”, frightened and sure by morning, and patient until the dog and her daughter came round

groups.label: Lighter for knowing Pepper will not be left waiting when she dies
groups.description: A dog likely to outlive her, provided for in her will, so the picture of her waiting at the window can be put down

groups.label: “Like having the lights on”: the house alive again

quoted.Initial:37:0: "Only that I didn't expect it. Any of it. … She opened the door, really, that's what it is. I was shut in and she opened the door. Some mornings I'd still rather she hadn't, when it's sleeting. But mostly I'm glad."
quoted.Initial:17:0: "She thought she was looking after me, and she was, I know she was. But it felt like she was taking something off me. Like I was a child who'd been given a puppy and couldn't be trusted with it."
quoted.Initial:31:0: "When I go to the shops she's at the window when I come back. Every time. … And I couldn't bear the thought of her doing that and me never coming."
